payload.name: Extract Third-Party Assessments Separately
payload.description: When a message contains both an explicit third-party assessment (e.g., doctor's statement, professional opinion) and a person's attitude or emotion, extract the assessment as its own candidate.
content: During extraction, when a speaker reports an explicit factual statement from another person (e.g., a doctor's assessment, diagnosis, or prognosis) while also expressing an attitude or emotion, create a separate memory candidate for the factual statement, preserving the source and exact content.
Do not let a summarizing state memory about the person's attitude (e.g., 'staying positive') replace or absorb the explicit third-party statement.
During CRUD, if an existing memory contains the attitude but omits the stated assessment, update or merge it to include the assessment rather than leaving the incomplete version.
Stop after capturing the assessment and the attitude; do not add inferred medical details, unstated severity, or speculative outcomes.

solves: Prevents loss of explicit third-party factual statements (e.g., professional assessments, diagnoses, or prognoses) when extraction focuses on a person's attitude or emotional state, by requiring such statements to be captured as separate memory candidates.
